s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive asthenia, anorexia, and weight loss with hypercalcemia and renal failure
salient_findings: Progressive asthenia, anorexia, and 7-kg weight loss
key_facts: 53-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and bipolar disorder
Acute functional renal failure (creatinine clearance 30 mL/min)
No monoclonal peak on serum or urine immunoelectrophoresis
Received IV saline and one dose of zoledronate with initial improvement
CT scan showed osteolytic lesions and hepatic and splenic nodules
Brain MRI showed T2-hyperintense, T1-isointense, gadolinium-enhancing lesions
DEXA scan revealed osteopenia (lumbar spine T-score –2.4)
Mammography, esophagogastroduodenoscopy, and colonoscopy were normal
Bone marrow biopsy and labial salivary gland histology were unremarkable
Percutaneous fine-needle aspiration of the liver showed noncaseating granulomatous hepatitis

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Hypercalcemia, renal failure, and polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia

shortlist.label: Malignancy-associated hypercalcemia
shortlist.why_kept: Osteolytic lesions, hepatic and splenic nodules, and hypercalcemia

raw.rationale: The presence of noncaseating granulomatous hepatitis, osteolytic lesions, and hypercalcemia with low PTH levels, along with the patient's overall clinical presentation, are consistent with sarcoidosis, a systemic granulomatous disease that can cause hypercalcemia due to increased vitamin D production by activated macrophages within granulomas.

rejected.label: Multiple Myeloma
rejected.why: The absence of a monoclonal peak on serum or urine immunoelectrophoresis and a normal serum free light-chain ratio make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: While lymphoma can cause hypercalcemia and granulomatous reactions, the specific findings of noncaseating granulomatous hepatitis and the lack of other specific lymphoma indicators make this less likely.

rejected.label: Granulomatous disease-associated hypercalcemia
rejected.why: This is more of a description of the condition rather than a specific diagnosis; sarcoidosis is a specific disease that fits this description.

rejected.label: Malignancy-associated hypercalcemia
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of malignancy from the provided diagnostic tests, such as mammography, esophagogastroduodenoscopy, colonoscopy, and bone marrow biopsy, which were all unremarkable or normal.
